survey: Image 5 shows a DJ controller and a pair of headphones on an orange surface. The controller is one blue body on a darker base plate, viewed from above at an angle. It has three sections: a left deck, a raised centre mixer and a right deck. Each deck has a large grey jog wheel set into the top, a small red display, a group of coloured pads at the top and a row of coloured buttons along the front edge. The centre mixer is a step higher than the decks. It has a light-blue screen on a raised block at the back, three round knobs, and fader caps sitting in slots. The joins between the sections step cleanly and the whole unit sits flat on the base plate, with a shadow under it. The two decks are not exact copies of each other, but their layouts are close and sensible. The headphones lie on the floor in front and to the right. The headband is one continuous arc whose ends meet yokes that hold both ear cups. One cup faces the camera with its padded opening showing; the other is turned so its outer side shows, as happens when headphones are put down with the cups swivelled. There is no cable, so these read as wireless headphones and nothing hangs loose. The faders are simplified (no clear horizontal crossfader), which is an acceptable game-art simplification, not a fault.
